thread:
nina: quick ping — i'm wireframing a "threshold orchestration" flow for SLOs in the console. goal: keep alerts meaningful while preventing notify storms when many tenants' thresholds shift. high-level idea: compute a proposed_threshold per-tenant, then pass it through a global "notify_budget_smoother" before applying to routing. thoughts?

omar: important to separate detection vs routing. proposed_threshold can be computed aggressively; smoother decides how much gets applied to notify fanout based on global budget and recent apply rate.

priya: agree. propose three decoupled stages: 1) compute_proposal (per-tenant), 2) local_gate (min_samples, abs_cap, hysteresis), 3) global_smoother (budget, rate_limit, backpressure). show all three in console with status badges.

nina: that maps well to UI: show "proposal" row and an "effective_threshold" row that will be used by notify. also surfacing why a proposal was rejected or damped (e.g., low samples, smoothed due to budget).

omar: for telemetry, emit events: proposal_generated, local_gate_decision, smooth_apply_attempt, smooth_reject_reason. dashboard panels: global_budget_utilization, applied_vs_proposed_delta_histogram, per-tenant_hysteresis_state.

priya: what should the smoother policy look like? i sketched a token-bucket style budget per-region + a fractional dampening parameter that decays if we haven't used budget recently. config keys: budget_tokens_per_hour, apply_cost_per_tenant (function of fanout_change), dampen_factor_initial, dampen_recovery_half_life.

nina: love the token-bucket idea. also add an emergency threshold: if notify_service_latency or error_rate > X, smoother immediately pauses all applies and signals ops. need a console kill-switch.

omar: small nuance: apply_cost isn't linear with delta_pct. a tiny percent change on a big tenant can be huge fanout. use estimated_fanout_delta = current_fanout * (delta_pct) as cost. precompute fanout estimate in proposal stage.

priya: i'll add min_apply_cost so micro-changes on tiny tenants don't consume budget. also suggestion: allow per-org opt-in so customers can choose aggressive autotune or conservative mode. surface that as a toggle in org settings.

slo-bot: scheduled simulation cohort: smoothing-sim-2026-04 cohort=4% start=1822227000 duration=48h. results will include simulated_budget_chart and proposal_vs_effective_ts.

ops-bot: note: alerting backpressure hook created at /infra/ops/hooks/notify-backpressure. will send channel alerts and set a console banner when active.

nina: rollout plan: 1) simulation 48h (no routing), 2) run soft-apply mode for small cohort where effective_threshold is weighted toward current (weight=0.2) for 24h, 3) if applied_vs_proposed median delta < 10% and no spike in notify queue, gradually increase weight. will document in RFC and add safety kill-switch.

omar: add analytic: fraction_of_tenants_in_local_fallback to detect too many low-sample tenants; if > threshold, pause and alert product.

priya: i'll prototype smoother lib and a small simulator to validate policies against historical traces. plan to push a draft RFC after simulation starts. tagging @nina @omar for review.

nina: thanks team — excited to see the sim data. will add console mocks for proposal vs effective rows and an audit trail link. :thumbsup:
